column1: # mapping_set_description: Manually curated alignment of the Mellea LinkML schema (linkml/src/mellea/schema/mellea.yaml) to the MITRE ATT&CK LinkML schema (linkml/src/mellea/mappings/attack/). Subjects are Mellea schema elements (classes and enum permissible values); objects are concepts from the ATT&CK schema. Mappings express conceptual alignment only -- the schemas have very different modelling intents (Mellea = AI runtime/code architecture; ATT&CK = adversary tactics/techniques knowledge base). Most alignments are weak (skos:relatedMatch); the strongest links are around runtime telemetry/observability and audit-mode plugins.

column8: Mellea runtime telemetry sources are conceptually analogous to ATT&CK DataSources that feed detection analytics.
Hook payloads carry granular runtime observation data, akin to ATT&CK DataComponents that decompose a DataSource into observable fields.
Plugins (especially audit-mode) execute custom logic over lifecycle events; ATT&CK Analytics encode detection logic over observable events. Weak structural analogue.
Audit-mode plugins implement runtime governance checks; DetectionStrategy describes a strategy for detecting adversary behaviour.
Both enumerate phases of an execution flow; semantics differ (AI runtime lifecycle vs adversary kill chain).
Mellea CLI commands are software tools; ATT&CK Tool models commercial/legitimate software an adversary may use. Surface-only name match.
Both are abstract roots for named, identifiable entities in their respective schemas.
Both are top-level container/bundle classes that aggregate the artefacts of one analysis or release.
Backend families denote model-serving infrastructure; ATT&CK Infrastructure describes adversary-controlled compute. Very weak link.
